scenario.title: Three-task round-robin kernel on the SysTick
scenario.description: The final checkpoint of weeks 7-9. main builds three task stacks (A blinks the LED, B prints the alphabet through the write system call, C counts and yields), programs the MPU with a guard below each stack, starts SysTick at one tick per 2000 cycles and executes "svc #0". The SVC handler returns into task A as an unprivileged thread on the PSP. Every tick pends PendSV, whose handler saves r4-r11, asks the scheduler for the next task and restores its registers. The run stops after 30 ticks.

expected.summary: 30 ticks, 40+ context switches, all tasks alive, the alphabet appears on the UART, the LED toggles, stack watermarks around 25 percent, no faults.

scenario.what_to_look_for: After main_entered: four task_state events (A, B, C and idle created, each with its stack range and initial PSP), an mpu event listing eight non-overlapping regions, the SysTick programming event (PendSV priority 0xFF reads back as 0xF0: four priority bits), then svc #0: exception_entry for SVCall from main, "svc start" with CONTROL=3, and an exception_return "back to thread mode (unprivileged)" from the PSP. From then on every 2000 cycles: irq_pend SysTick, exception_entry SysTick with EXC_RETURN 0xFFFFFFFD (frame pushed on the task's PSP), irq_pend PendSV, "SysTick returning, but PendSV is pending: tail-chain", tail_chain PendSV, context_switch A->B with both PSPs, exception_return into B. Task C yields with svc #1, so its slices are short. The viewer timeline shows A, B, C in rotation with thin handler strips between them; click a context_switch to see every suspended task's saved frame. summary.kernel_timing gives the switch cost (about 56 cycles: tail-chain, 8-register save and restore, scheduler, unstacking) and the tick handler cost. summary.kernel.tasks.*.watermark.percent is about 25 (the 64-byte initial frame on a 256-byte stack). The tick is 2000 cycles only to keep the trace short; a real kernel ticks at about 1 kHz (150000 cycles at 150 MHz).
likely_root_causes: Healthy baseline. Compare with P07/P08/P09 for the broken variants.
If your board shows no switching: SysTick not enabled (CSR bits), TICKINT clear, or PendSV not pended from the tick handler.
If the first task never starts: the initial frame is built in the wrong order, the xPSR word is missing the Thumb bit, or EXC_RETURN is 0xFFFFFFF9 instead of 0xFFFFFFFD.
how_to_debug: Break in PendSV_Handler and print the PSP and the 16 words above it; they must match the TCB layout diagram (r4-r11 then the hardware frame).
Toggle a different GPIO pin in each task and watch the three square waves interleave on the scope at the tick period.
Check ICSR after the tick handler: PENDSVSET must be 1 until PendSV runs.
Count switches per second in a global and print it once a second; compare with ticks per second.
scenario.what_this_means: A preemptive kernel is a timer interrupt, a lowest-priority exception that does the switch, and a stack per task that holds the task's registers while it is not running. The hardware frame is pushed by the core for free; the kernel only adds r4-r11 and swaps PSP. Everything in the trace between two context_switch events is one time slice.
scenario.hidden_symptom: LED blinks, alphabet scrolls, counter increments; three things happen at once on one core.
